name: Ramp
text: We should add a visible server-side skip link at the top of every page, allowing all users to bypass navigation. This decision prioritizes inclusivity for screen reader and keyboard users, who may struggle with repetitive navigation. By doing this, we're accepting the potential trade-off of added visual clutter for sighted users, but it's a worthwhile sacrifice for making the site usable for everyone. This approach also aligns with our quality-first principle, ensuring a solid foundation for accessibility.

name: Reader
text: I'm flagging the server-side skip link idea because it forces every user to download and parse an extra element, which may not be necessary for most users. A better alternative is to implement a client-side solution, but with a fallback for JavaScript-disabled or slow-loading scenarios. To settle this, I need to see data on how many users rely on screen readers or keyboard navigation versus those who would be slowed down by the extra element, and consider a solution that balances these competing needs.
